title: Injective module sheaves are acyclic as abelian sheaves on every object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $I$ be an injective object of the category $\Mod(X_{\Et},R)$ of sheaves of $R_X$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; write $I_{ab}\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ for its underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For an object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ let $H^q(U,-)$ be the $q$-th right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab$, $G\mapsto G(U)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive] (cohomology computed in abelian sheaves, not in modules). Then $H^q(U,I_{ab})=0$ for every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every $q>0$. ($I_{ab}$ need not be an injective abelian sheaf: the left adjoint $G\mapsto G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R_X$ of the forgetful functor is not exact in general.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), second paragraph of the proof: Lemma Tag 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection) with $\mathcal B=\mathcal C$ and all coverings, its assumption (3) given by Lemma Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech), which rests on Lemma Tag 03FB (lemma-injective-module-injective-presheaf); stated there for any ringed site

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $U$ in $X_{\Et}$. Write $\mathcal O=R_X$ and, as in [lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact], $\mathcal O_V$ for the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $W\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\Mor(W,V)}\mathcal O(W)$ and $K_\bullet=\mathcal O_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ for the chain complex with $K_p=\bigoplus_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}\mathcal O_{U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}}$ and alternating differential. For any presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and object $V$, a morphism $\psi:\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal G$ is determined by $\psi_V(1\cdot[\mathrm{id}_V])\in\mathcal G(V)$, and every element $g\in\mathcal G(V)$ arises, from $\psi_W(a\cdot[\varphi])=a\,\varphi^*g$ (Yoneda); so $\Hom_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal O_V,\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(V)$, naturally in $V$ and $\mathcal G$, and $\Hom(\bigoplus_\alpha\mathcal O_{V_\alpha},\mathcal G)=\prod_\alpha\mathcal G(V_\alpha)$. Under these identifications the map $\Hom(K_p,\mathcal G)\to\Hom(K_{p+1},\mathcal G)$ induced by the differential of $K_\bullet$ is $s\mapsto(\sum_j(-1)^js_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_{p+1}}})$, because the map $\mathcal O_{V'}\to\mathcal O_V$ induced by a morphism $V'\to V$ corresponds to restriction $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V')$. Hence $\Hom_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(K_\bullet,\mathcal G)\cong\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$ as cochain complexes [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex], functorially in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech), proof, first display: Lemma Tag 03AS (lemma-cech-map-into), whose proof is the tautology of Modules on Sites, Lemma Tag 03A8 (lemma-obvious-adjointness), combined with the change-of-rings adjunction Modules on Sites, Lemma Tag 03CU (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict-presheaves) for Z_{U,bullet} tensor_{p,Z} O

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact] applied to the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O=R_X$ and the covering $\mathcal U$, the complex $K_\bullet$ is exact in positive degrees in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$: $H_p(K_\bullet)=0$ for $p>0$ (exactness in the presheaf category is objectwise).

Let $I$ be injective in $\Mod(X_{\Et},R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-injective-presheaf], $I$ is injective in $\mathrm{PMod}(R_X)$, so the contravariant functor $\Hom_{\mathrm{PMod}(R_X)}(-,I)$ is exact; an exact additive functor commutes with taking homology, so $H^p(\Hom(K_\bullet,I))=\Hom(H_p(K_\bullet),I)=0$ for $p>0$ by the previous step. By the first step this cochain complex is $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,I)$; thus $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I)=0$ for every $p>0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech), proof: Lemma Tag 03FB and exactness of Hom(-, I)

proof.text: The Cech complex of the module sheaf $I$ is by definition [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] the Cech complex of its underlying presheaf of abelian groups, which is the underlying presheaf of the abelian sheaf $I_{ab}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] (same groups $I(V)$, same restriction maps). Hence $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I_{ab})=\check H^p(\mathcal U,I)=0$ for $p>0$, for every covering $\mathcal U$ of every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), proof, second paragraph: assumption (3) of Lemma 03F9 holds by Lemma 03FC

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion] to $\mathcal F=I_{ab}$, $\mathcal B=\Ob(X_{\Et})$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of all coverings of $X_{\Et}$. Assumption (1) holds because fibre products of objects of $X_{\Et}$ over an object exist in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; assumption (2) holds because every covering of $U$ belongs to $\mathrm{Cov}$ and refines itself; assumption (3) is the previous step. The criterion gives $H^q(U,I_{ab})=0$ for every $q>0$ and every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$, cohomology being the derived functors of $G\mapsto G(U)$ on $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, which is the claim.

split_report.summary: Statement kept: it is the second paragraph of the proof of Stacks 03FD for the ringed site (X_et, R_X), and cohomology is taken in Ab(X_et) as there. Proof written from Stacks sites-cohomology: steps 1-3 write out the proof of 03FC (the Cech complex of I is Hom_{PMod(R_X)}(K_bullet, I) for the complex K_bullet of free presheaves of R_X-modules of the covering (03AS + 03CU, Yoneda, elementary); K_bullet is exact in positive degrees (03AT/03F5, new node lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact, unsplit); I is injective among presheaves of modules (03FB, new node lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-injective-presheaf, a Mathlib leaf via the sheafification adjunction of presheaves of modules and preservesInjectiveObjects_of_adjunction_of_preservesMonomorphisms), so Hom(-, I) is exact); step 4 passes from I to I_ab (same Cech complex); step 5 applies the Cech criterion 03F9 (new node lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion, stated as Stacks states it, with B and Cov, unsplit) with B = all objects and Cov = all coverings. The existing lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion (imported, unit sk-thm-properbasechange, not reviewed) was not used: it assumes every covering of a basis object has a finite basis refinement and concludes only for basis objects, which fails for non-quasi-compact objects of X_et with B = all objects (and with B = affine objects it gives only affine U, while the user lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-direct-image-acyclic needs U = X x_S V arbitrary); its unit is also not cited by sk-thm-p1, and its second step has elementary null. New definition def-weil-pbc-cech-complex (Cech complex for an arbitrary family, Stacks 03AM), a Mathlib leaf via cechComplexFunctor on Over U; def-weil-pbc-cover-cech is its finite special case. Mathlib searched three ways for the item and each new node.
